verses.gurmukhi: ਸੁਣੀ ਪੁਕਾਰਿ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਗੁਰੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਗ ਮਾਹਿ ਪਠਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: sunee pukaar dhaataar prabh gur naanak jag maeh paThaiaa|

en.bdb: The benefactor Lord listened to the cries (of humanity) and sent Guru Nanak to this world.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚਰਨ ਧੋਇ ਰਹਰਾਸਿ ਕਰਿ ਚਰਣਾਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸਿਖਾਂ ਪੀਲਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: charan dhoi raharaas kar charanaamrit sikhaa(n) peelaiaa|

en.bdb: He washed His feet, eulogised God and got his Disciples drink the ambrosia of his feet.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਪੂਰਨ ਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਕਲਿਜੁਗਿ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਇਕੁ ਦਿਖਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: paarabraham pooran braham kalijug a(n)dhar ik dhikhaiaa|

en.bdb: He preached in this darkage (kaliyug) that, saragun (Brahm) and nirgun (Parbrahm) are the same and identical.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚਾਰੇ ਪੈਰ ਧਰੱਮ ਦੇ ਚਾਰਿ ਵਰਨਿ ਇਕੁ ਵਰਨੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: chaare pair dhara'm dhe chaar varan ik varan karaiaa|

en.bdb: Dharma was now established on its four feet and all the four castes (through fraternal feeling) were converted into one caste (of  humanity).

verses.gurmukhi: ਰਾਣਾ ਰੰਕੁ ਬਰਾਬਰੀ ਪੈਰੀ ਪਾਵਣਾ ਜਗਿ ਵਰਤਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: raanaa ra(n)k baraabaree pairee paavanaa jag varataiaa|

en.bdb: Equating the poor with the prince, he spread the etiquette of humbly touching the feet.

verses.gurmukhi: ਉਲਟਾ ਖੇਲੁ ਪਿਰੰਮ ਦਾ ਪੈਰਾ ਉਪਰਿ ਸੀਸੁ ਨਿਵਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: aulaTaa khel pira(n)m dhaa pairaa upar sees nivaiaa|

en.bdb: Inverse is the game of the beloved; he got the egotist high heads bowed to feet.

verses.gurmukhi: ਕਲਿਜੁਗੁ ਬਾਬੇ ਤਾਰਿਆ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਪੜ੍ਹਿ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੁ ਸੁਣਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: kalijug baabe taariaa sat naam paReh ma(n)tr sunaiaa|

en.bdb: Baba Nanak liberated this dark age (kaljug) and recited the mantra of satnaam for one and all.
Guru Nanak came to redeem the kaliyug.
